subject.title: fix(streaming): preserve paragraph separators across block-streamed deliveries [AI-assisted]

question: Should the permanent block-streaming contract preserve paragraph boundaries as in-band text on chunks, carry explicit boundary metadata through delivery, or accept a limited text-only repair for common cases?
rationale: The bug and owner boundary are clear, but this PR’s discussion and source path show the near-`maxChars` case cannot be completed by the current text-only shape without a maintainer choice about the streaming delivery contract.

options.title: Consolidate a complete shared fix
options.body: Choose one candidate or replacement and require it to preserve paragraph boundaries across both ordinary and near-`maxChars` splits before merge.

options.title: Adopt explicit boundary metadata
options.body: Ask contributors to carry paragraph/newline/hard-split seam metadata through the chunker, subscriber, and coalescer if in-band text cannot satisfy all invariants.

options.title: Accept a partial text-only repair
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally land the common-case separator fix while leaving the near-limit boundary documented as remaining work on the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Consolidate a complete shared fix
recommendation.body: Choose one candidate or replacement and require it to preserve paragraph boundaries across both ordinary and near-`maxChars` splits before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest recent history on the current chunker/coalescer layout and is a good routing owner for the delivery-contract choice.
